payload.title: Generic FrickStore<Model> observable object cache + sync loop
payload.description:
## Frick today
FrickClient exposes one-shot/imperative verbs: fetchObjects(type:), writeObject(...), deleteObject(...), and socket.subscribeObject(type:) emitting raw .objectsDelta frames. Nothing holds the results, nothing re-renders SwiftUI, nothing reconciles a delta into a cache.

## What RangerCRM built (port source of truth)
/Users/bri/dev/RangerCRM/RangerCRM/Model/RangerData/Stores/FrickAccountStore.swift (and 15 near-identical siblings). Each is an @MainActor @Observable cache that:
- bootstrap(): fetch + map to model + sort, then open the sync socket
- startSyncSubscription(): connectSync, subscribeObject(type:), consume .objectsDelta, and on any touching delta call refetchOnDelta()
- refetchOnDelta(): re-fetch via REST and MERGE IN PLACE (removeAll absent ids, then mergeIntoCache per row) so ForEach rebinds same-id rows instead of replacing instances
- upsert / delete: write-through to the server then update the cache
- reset(): tear down on sign-out
- a `static weak var bridge` pointer the DataController bridge reads through

Every one of the 16 files is this same ~220 lines; the ONLY per-entity differences are the DTO type and the sort predicate.

Note the two hard-won correctness fixes embedded as ///FIX comments in FrickAccountStore.swift:
- line ~157: re-sort/re-emit on every merge so an in-place edit (which mutates a model but not the array) still triggers @FrickQuery re-render
- line ~210: in-place merge on delta refetch so cross-device edits re-render existing cells rather than replacing instances (ForEach won't rebind a same-id row)
These must be preserved in the generic version — they are exactly the bugs the next app would re-hit.

## What the port gives us
The whole .objectsDelta -> live SwiftUI loop becomes framework-owned. Each app store collapses from ~220 lines to ~10 (DTO type + sort). ~3,500 LOC of RangerCRM -> one generic class. New entities become nearly free. The subtle re-render/delete-reconciliation fixes live in ONE place instead of 16.

## Shape (sketch)
```swift
@MainActor @Observable
open class FrickStore<Model: FrickModel> {
    public private(set) var items: [Model]
    public private(set) var hasBootstrapped: Bool
    public private(set) var lastError: String?
    // injected: client/session, DTO type, sort, model factory
    open func bootstrap() async { ... }
    open func upsert(_ dto: Model.DTO) async { ... }
    open func delete(id: String) async { ... }
    open func reset() { ... }
}
```
App side: `final class FrickAccountStore: FrickStore<AccountFrickModel> { sort = { ... } }` — DTO + sort only.

Depends on the FrickModel protocol contract (see the model-macro story for the wrapper; the protocol itself can land here). Decide whether the `static weak var bridge` registry is part of this story or the registry story — they're coupled.

## Downstream impact
RangerCRM: replace 16 hand-written Frick*Store files with thin subclasses. Highest value, lowest risk port of the epic — do it first to prove the FrickModel contract.
